status: draft: demonstration values, validate with NASA HRP sources and a physician

causes.label: Hypoxia or asphyxia risk from depressurization / O2 supply failure
causes.description: Peripheral oxygen saturation drop compromising cellular and tissue oxygenation.
causes.criterion: SpO2 below normal threshold (< 95%, or < 90% at altitude), or reported dyspnea at rest / suffocation.

causes.label: Cardiovascular strain and metabolic fatigue during EVA
causes.description: Disproportionate cardiac exertion relative to maximal physical capacity in the spacesuit.
causes.criterion: EVA environment with heart rate exceeding 80% of estimated HR max (208 - 0.7 * age) or respiratory rate > 30 bpm.

causes.label: Cephalad fluid shift (Space adaptation syndrome)
causes.description: Rostral migration of 1.5–2 L of blood and interstitial fluid due to loss of the hydrostatic gradient in early microgravity.
causes.criterion: Days 1–3 of microgravity exposure with reported frontal headache or facial congestion (not linked to arterial hypertension).
causes.clinical_note: Validate with NASA HRP sources: physiological fluid shift affects ~80% of crew in early flight days.

causes.label: Orthostatic intolerance from spaceflight hypovolemia
causes.description: Cardiovascular maladaptation with perfusion pressure drop on positional or gravitational stress.
causes.criterion: Systolic BP < 95 mmHg or diastolic BP < 60 mmHg with compensatory tachycardia or pre-syncope symptoms.

causes.label: Hyperthermia or active infectious process
causes.description: Core body temperature elevation from environmental heat accumulation or pyrogenic response.
causes.criterion: Core temperature > 37.5 C at rest or > 38.3 C (critical range).

causes.label: Reactive blood pressure elevation or hemodynamic overload
causes.description: Hyperreactive vascular response associated with mission stress, fluid overload, or vasoconstriction.
causes.criterion: Systolic BP >= 136 mmHg or diastolic BP >= 89 mmHg at rest.
